videos.script: Two departments share one floor and one switch. Finance and the warehouse, say. Every broadcast one of them sends, the other one hears. {{one-lan}} The obvious fix is a second switch. The cheaper one is a VLAN: the same switch, split in two by its configuration. A port in VLAN 10 and a port in VLAN 20 behave as if they were on different switches. {{split}} In this lesson you will split a small network into two VLANs, port by port. And you will see it break, because the cable between the two switches only knows one VLAN. {{break}} Then you will turn that cable into a trunk, which carries both. You will see the four bytes the switch adds to every frame on it, and watch them disappear before the frame reaches a PC. {{tag}} Last, you will configure the two ends of a trunk so that they disagree. Two VLANs leak into each other, and nothing complains. Then you will fix it the way it should have been set up from the start. {{native}} The lab is two switches and five PCs, built on one Linux computer. Every command ran, and every output is the one it printed. {{lab}}
